changes.evidence: Both stages are backstory. Addison's U.S. Army service was in World War I, 15 years before the show. Episode 2 says he and Marko 'once worked as enforcers for Silvermane' (past tense). By the time he appears in episode 1 (1933), Cat Hardy has hired him to burn down Silvermane's mansion, Silvermane's man Winston is paying PIs to hunt him, and Donegal kills him. He belongs to no group during the show, so the Army, Silvermane and Independent stages all go (the Independent stage only records leaving the backstory mob).

Derik's S.H.I.E.L.D. service (as an assassin, then a T.A.H.I.T.I. test subject) ended before the show: S.H.I.E.L.D. wiped his memory and gave him a new identity years earlier. In episode 29 (S2E7, 'The Writing on the Wall') he is a former agent hunting other T.A.H.I.T.I. patients and is taken into custody. He is not a member at any point on screen, so the S.H.I.E.L.D. stage and the Independent stage that follows it both go.

Demidov is 'a former Soviet Armed Forces soldier' (478th Regiment, Battle of Finow, WWII). That service is backstory. In Agent Carter S1 (1946) he is only a Leviathan operative, and he dies in episode 2.

In episode 61 (S3E17, 'The Team'), after Hive kills his daughter and S.H.I.E.L.D. captures him, Malick 'agreed to work with S.H.I.E.L.D. and betray Hydra'. He gives Coulson the intel that lets Talbot strike HYDRA, and Daisy (sent by Hive) kills him for betraying HYDRA. That is a defection, not just captivity. He becomes an informant, not an agent, so the new stage is Independent.

owner_calls.question: Does Scorch leave Centipede in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. episode 5 when he breaks out of its lab and kills its scientist Debbie Hynes?
options: Yes: add ['Independent', 'Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S1'] as the last stage
No: he was being held, keep the current stages
owner_calls.evidence: Raina recruits Chan, but then Centipede captures him, injects him and starts draining his blood. Raina 'was just using him'. He escapes the lab, incinerates Debbie Hynes and 'attack[s] S.H.I.E.L.D. agents and Centipede Project members alike' before May kills him. The wiki says Centipede's betrayal 'caus[ed] him to go rogue', but it all happens while he is effectively a captive, and the owner's rules say captivity is not a move.

owner_calls.question: Does Masters break from the Council of Nine in Agent Carter episode 17 when he joins Thompson, Sousa and Carter in a plot to kill its new leader, Whitney Frost?
options: Yes: add ['Independent', 'Agent Carter S2'] as the last stage
No: it is a power struggle inside the Council, keep the current stages
owner_calls.evidence: After Frost kills the other members and takes over the Council, Masters makes a deal with Thompson, Sousa and Carter to repair the Gamma Cannon and kill Frost (S2E9, 'A Little Song and Dance'). He tries to shoot her, but Thompson betrays him to her. Even while being drained, he pleads that his connections make him her more valuable ally, so it is unclear whether he means to leave the Council or take it over.
